lgd_definition: “Working/Livestock Guardian Dog” means a dog that is specifically trained to work and/or live with domestic farm animals (i.e. cattle, sheep, goats, etc.) without causing them harm while aggressively repelling predators.
collar_tag_req: The dog owner shall keep the metal tag securely fixed on the dog at all times or until the tag is renewed or replaced except when the dog is engaged in a lawful hunting activity.
dog_limit: 2 dogs per household, but up to 5 dogs per agricultural location.
notes: Farm-friendly bylaw. It features a specific definition for 'Working/Livestock Guardian Dog' and sets a higher limit of 5 dogs per agricultural location (compared to 2 dogs for a standard household). LGDs are subject to a separate annual block fee ($100 for up to 5 dogs) rather than individual standard tag fees, and are exempt from 'running at large' provisions while actively working on their owner’s premises. However, the by-law explicitly states working/livestock guardian dogs are not entirely exempt from the Animal Control By-law itself.

collar_tag_req: All dogs must be registered and always wear their dog tag. The tag is issued by the Director and must be securely affixed to the dog.
dog_limit: Households within village limits are permitted two (2) dogs. Households outside village limits are permitted three (3) dogs.
notes: Standard animal care and control by-law. There is a general limit difference based on zoning (3 dogs permitted outside village limits vs. 2 inside village limits), but there are no specific definitions or exemptions for livestock guardian dogs or working farm dogs.

lgd_definition: “Livestock Guardian Dog” (LGD) shall mean a dog that works and/or lives with domestic farm animals such as cattle, sheep and poultry to protect them while repelling predators and is used on land legally used for exclusively for that purpose.
herding_definition: “Herding Dog” means a dog that has been trained and is actively being used on land legally used for a bona fide farming operation for the purposes of controlling livestock on the farm.
collar_tag_req: The Municipality issues Dog Tag Licences (no annual fees, just a nominal one-time processing fee of $10.00). The Dog Tag must be worn by the animal at all times.
dog_limit: Maximum 2 dogs per dwelling unit or premises. Exemption: "Notwithstanding section 3.1 of this by-law, more than two (2) livestock guardian dogs and/or herding dogs may be licensed for lawful livestock operations on agricultural premises."
notes: Highly farm-friendly by-law. Includes explicit definitions for both 'Livestock Guardian Dog' and 'Herding Dog', and completely exempts them from the two-dog limit provided they are on agricultural premises and a clearly visible warning sign is posted at the entrance(s).

lgd_definition: “Working Dog” shall mean any of various breeds of dogs developed or trained to perform useful work to assist humans (i.e. herding animals, pulling wagons or sleds, livestock guardian, or guarding property) and excludes hunting dogs.
collar_tag_req: Every dog Owner shall cause a dog tag to be securely affixed on the dog at all times (until the tag needs replaced).
dog_limit: Maximum of 3 dogs on a single detached dwelling. Exemption: Sections 3.8.1 and 3.8.2 shall not apply to a property which is zoned Agricultural, a property possessing a valid kennel license, an approved business and/or veterinary offices.
notes: Farm-friendly bylaw. Defines "Working Dog" broadly to include both livestock guardians and herding dogs. Explicitly exempts properties zoned as Agricultural from the 3-dog limit, making it favourable for farming operations. Noise/barking is enforced under a separate noise by-law.

collar_tag_req: An owner of a dog shall keep the tag issued by the Town securely fixed on the dog it was issued at all times. No person shall affix a tag to any dog other than the dog for which it was issued; or remove a tag except to replace it with a current or valid tag.
dog_limit: No person shall keep or harbour or permit to be kept or harboured at any one time, more than three (3) dogs on a property or per dwelling unit.
notes: Standard urban animal control by-law. While there are specific definitions and licensing exemptions for Service Dogs and Police Working Dogs, there are no definitions or exemptions for farm dogs, herding dogs, or livestock guardian dogs.

collar_tag_req: Every dog owner within the City’s limits shall obtain a dog licence annually by the first day of January of each year.
dog_limit: No person shall harbour more than three (3) dogs in an urban area, and no more than five (5) dogs in a rural area.
notes: Note: The document linked in the prompt (16-139) is the Animal Regulation By-law primarily dealing with exotic/prohibited animals. Dog control is governed by the Dog Licensing and Control By-law (15-034). It is farm-friendly because it explicitly allows a higher limit of 5 dogs in rural areas compared to 3 dogs in urban areas, though there are no specific LGD definitions.

lgd_definition: Working/Livestock Guardian Dog - shall mean a dog that is specifically trained and actively being used in a bona-fide farming operation, to work and/or live with domestic farm animals (i.e. cattle, sheep, etc.) to protect and/or control them while aggressively repelling predators and is used exclusively for that
collar_tag_req: Working/Livestock Guardian Dogs shall be exempt from wearing a collar or tag, provided that the Owner has paid the annual licensing fee, registered said dog with the Township and provided identifying information for the dog from a registered micro-chip.
dog_limit: Maximum of 2 dogs per household. Exemption: "Notwithstanding the limit set forth in Section 5.2.1, a person may own, harbor, keep or permit to be kept an additional three (3) dogs at a premise provided the dogs are working/livestock guardian dogs."
notes: Extremely farm-friendly by-law, incorporating recent amendments. It specifically defines Working/Livestock Guardian Dogs, exempts them from wearing collars/tags while working (provided they are microchipped and licensed), and exempts them from noise/barking bylaw provisions while actively engaged in their duties. It also increases the limit from 2 dogs to 5 dogs strictly to accommodate 3 additional working/livestock guardian dogs for owners with domestic farm animals.

collar_tag_req: Effective January 1, 2022, residents are no longer required to purchase a municipal dog tag. Each owner is to obtain their own tag with owner contact information clearly displayed (must include a phone number for the owner of the dog).
dog_limit: No person shall keep more than 3 dogs in any one dwelling unit or on any premises.
notes: The municipality removed municipal dog tag and licensing fees entirely for all dogs as of 2022, requiring owners to self-tag. "Guard Dog" is defined, but is restricted to security purposes on commercial/industrial land, not agricultural. No explicit mentions of working farm dogs or LGDs in the by-law.

collar_tag_req: The owner shall keep the dog tag securely fastened on the dog at all times until the tag is renewed or replaced, but the tag may be removed while the dog is lawfully hunting.
dog_limit: Not explicitly restricted for general households, though keeping more than 5 dogs constitutes a Kennel per the Township Zoning By-Law 2023-50.
notes: While there is no formal LGD definition, the by-law explicitly acknowledges and protects farm dogs in its running at large provisions: 'Farm dogs and hunting dogs under the control of any person and acting in accordance with acceptable behavior shall not be deemed to be running at large when found in any place other than the premises of the owner.'

collar_tag_req: All dogs must be licensed and wear an issued municipal tag.
dog_limit: Maximum of seven animals per household, including no more than three (3) dogs and four cats.
notes: Recently updated modern 'Responsible Pet Ownership and Animal Regulation' by-law. It outlines strict limits on household pets and introduces an Administrative Monetary Penalty System. There are no farm dog or livestock guardian dog provisions or exemptions, reflecting its urban nature.
